cues.en: Hi. I'm Herb Gross, and welcome to Calculus Revisited.
cues.zh: 大家好，我是 Herb Gross，欢迎来到《微积分再探》。

cues.en: I guess the most difficult lecture to give in any course is probably the first one, and you're sort of tempted to look at your audience and say, you're probably wondering why I called you all here.
cues.zh: 我想任何课程中最难讲的一堂课大概都是第一堂，你总会忍不住看着听众想说，你们大概在想我为什么把你们都叫来。

cues.en: And in this sense, I have elected to entitle our first lecture simply preface,
cues.zh: 从这个意义上说，我把第一讲直接命名为“前言”，

cues.en: to give a double overview,
cues.zh: 做一个双重概览，

cues.en: an overview both of the hardware and the software that will make up this course.
cues.zh: 既概览本课程的硬件，也概览其软件。

cues.en: To begin with,
cues.zh: 首先，

cues.en: we will have a series of lectures of which this is the first.
cues.zh: 我们会有一系列讲座，这是第一讲。

cues.en: In our lectures,
cues.zh: 在讲座中，

cues.en: our main aim will be to give an overview of the material being covered, an insight as to why various computations are done,
cues.zh: 我们的主要目标是概览所涵盖的内容，讲清楚各种计算为什么要这样做，

cues.en: and insights as to how applications of these concepts will be made.
cues.zh: 以及这些概念将如何应用。

cues.en: The heart of our course will consist of a regular textbook.
cues.zh: 本课程的核心将是一本常规教材。

cues.en: You
cues.zh: 你们

cues.en: see we have our lectures,
cues.zh: 看，我们有讲座，

cues.en: we have a textbook,
cues.zh: 我们有教材，

cues.en: the textbook is designed
cues.zh: 教材的设计

cues.en: to supply you with,
cues.zh: 是为了给你提供

cues.en: deeper insights than what we can give in a lecture.
cues.zh: 比课堂上能讲得更深入的见解。

cues.en: In addition, recognizing
cues.zh: 此外，考虑到

cues.en: the fact that the textbook
cues.zh: 教材

cues.en: may leave gaps, places where you may want some additional knowledge, we also have supplementary notes.
cues.zh: 可能留有空白，也就是你可能想补充知识的地方，我们还准备了补充讲义。

cues.en: And finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: at the backbone
cues.zh: 在我们课程包的核心位置

cues.en: of our package is what we call the study guide.
cues.zh: 是我们所说的学习指南。

cues.en: The study guide consists of a breakdown of the course. It tells us
cues.zh: 学习指南包含课程分解。它告诉我们

cues.en: what the various lectures will be, units. There are pretests
cues.zh: 各讲座和单元将是什么内容。其中有预测试

cues.en: to help you decide how well prepared you are for the topic that's coming up. There is a final examination
cues.zh: 帮助你判断自己对即将到来的主题准备得如何。还有期末考试

cues.en: at the end of each block of material.
cues.zh: 在每个材料模块结束时。

cues.en: And perhaps most importantly,
cues.zh: 也许最重要的是，

cues.en: especially from an engineer's point of view,
cues.zh: 尤其从工程师的角度看，

cues.en: in each unit that we study, the study guide will consist
cues.zh: 在我们学习的每个单元中，学习指南都会包含

cues.en: of exercises
cues.zh: 练习

cues.en: primarily called learning exercises.
cues.zh: 主要称为学习练习。

cues.en: Exercises which hopefully
cues.zh: 这些练习有望

cues.en: will turn you on towards wanting to be able to apply the material, and at the same time, serve as a springboard
cues.zh: 激发你去应用这些材料，同时作为跳板

cues.en: by which we can highlight why the theory and many of our lecture points are really as important as they are.
cues.zh: 借此强调为什么理论和我们许多讲座要点确实如此重要。

cues.en: So much for the hardware of our course. And now, let's turn our attention to the software.
cues.zh: 课程的“硬件”就讲到这里。现在，让我们把注意力转向“软件”。

cues.en: Just what is calculus?
cues.zh: 微积分到底是什么？

cues.en: In a manner of speaking,
cues.zh: 可以说，

cues.en: calculus can be viewed as being high school mathematics
cues.zh: 微积分可以看作高中数学

cues.en: with one additional concept called the limit concept thrown in. If you recall back to your high school days, remember that we were always dealing with things like average
cues.zh: 再加上一个称为极限的概念。回想高中时代，我们总是在处理像平均的

cues.en: constant rate of speed.
cues.zh: 恒定速度。

cues.en: The old recipe that distance equals rate times time
cues.zh: 距离等于速率乘以时间这个老公式

cues.en: presupposes that the rate is constant.
cues.zh: 预设了速率是恒定的。

cues.en: Because if the rate is varying, which rate is it that you use to multiply the time by to find the distance?
cues.zh: 因为如果速率在变化，你该用哪个速率乘以时间来求距离呢？

cues.en: You see, in other words, roughly speaking, we can say
cues.zh: 你看，换句话说，粗略来讲我们可以说

cues.en: that at least one branch of calculus known as differential calculus deals with the subject of instantaneous
cues.zh: 微积分中至少有一个分支——也就是微分学，研究的是瞬时

cues.en: speed. And instantaneous speed is a rather easy thing to talk about intuitively.
cues.zh: 速度。直观上讲，瞬时速度其实挺容易理解的。

cues.en: Imagine
cues.zh: 想象一下

cues.en: an object moving along this line and passing the point p.
cues.zh: 一个物体沿着这条线运动，穿过了点 p。

cues.en: And we say to ourselves, how fast was the object moving at the instant that we were at the point p.
cues.zh: 我们不禁会问，在到达点 p 的那一瞬间，物体的速度究竟有多快？

cues.en: Now you see, this is some sort of a problem because at the instant that you're at p,
cues.zh: 你看，这其实成了一个问题，因为在刚好处在 p 点的瞬间，

cues.en: you're not, in a sense, moving at all because you're at p.
cues.zh: 某种意义上你根本没在动，因为你就停在 p 点。

cues.en: Of course, what we do to reduce this new problem to an old one is we say, well, suppose we had a couple of observers. Let's call them o one and o two.
cues.zh: 当然，为了把这个新问题化归为已知问题，我们不妨假设有两位观察者，姑且称他们为 o1 和 o2。

cues.en: Let them be stationed one on each side of p. Now, certainly, what we can do physically here is we can measure the distance
cues.zh: 让他们分别守在 p 点的两侧。显然，在物理上我们完全可以测出

cues.en: between o one and o two.
cues.zh: o1 和 o2 之间的距离。

cues.en: And we can also measure the time
cues.zh: 而且我们也能测出

cues.en: that it takes to go from o one to o two.
cues.zh: 从 o1 运动到 o2 所花费的时间。

cues.en: And what we can do is divide that distance by the time, and that, you see, is our old high school concept of the average speed of the particle as it moves from o one to o two. Now, you see, the question is, somebody says, gee, that's a great answer, but it's the wrong problem. We didn't ask what was the average speed as we went from o one to o two. We asked what was the instantaneous speed. And the idea is we say, well, look it. The average speed and the instantaneous speed, it seems, should be pretty much the same if the observers were relatively close together.
cues.zh: 然后用距离除以时间，你看，这就是我们高中学过的粒子从 o1 移动到 o2 的平均速度概念。但问题在于，有人会说：哎呀，回答得很漂亮，但答非所问。我们问的不是从 o1 到 o2 的平均速度，而是瞬时速度。而我们的想法是：你看，如果这两位观察者靠得足够近，平均速度和瞬时速度按理说就应该差不多。

cues.en: The next observation is, it seems that if we were to move the observers in even closer,
cues.zh: 下一个观察是，如果我们把观察者移得更近，

cues.en: there would be less of a discrepancy
cues.zh: 差异就会更小

cues.en: between o one and o two in the sense that... Not a discrepancy, but in the sense that the average speed would now seem like a better approximation to the instantaneous speed because there was less distance for something to go wrong in.
cues.zh: 在 o1 和 o2 之间……不是差异，而是说平均速度看起来会更接近瞬时速度，因为出错的区间更短了。

cues.en: And so we get the idea that maybe what we should do is make the observers get closer and closer together.
cues.zh: 于是我们想到，也许应该让观察者越来越靠近。

cues.en: That would minimize the difference between average speed and the instantaneous rate of speed.
cues.zh: 这样就能把平均速度和瞬时速率之间的差异最小化。

cues.en: And maybe the optimal thing would happen when the two observers were together.
cues.zh: 也许最优的情况就是两个观察者重合在一起。

cues.en: But the strange part is, and this is where calculus really begins, this is what calculus is all about, as soon as the observers come together, notice that what you have is that the distance between them is zero, the time that it takes to get from one to the other is zero, and therefore it appears that if we divide distance by time, we are going to wind up with
cues.zh: 但奇怪的地方在于——这也是微积分真正的起点，微积分讲的就是这个——一旦观察者重合，注意此时它们之间的距离是零，从一个到另一个所需的时间也是零，因此看起来如果我们用距离除以时间，最终会得到

cues.en: zero over zero.
cues.zh: 零除以零。

cues.en: Now my claim is that zero over zero should be called...
cues.zh: 我的主张是，零除以零应该被称为……

cues.en: Well, I'll call it undefined.
cues.zh: 嗯，我会叫它未定义。

cues.en: But actually, I think indeterminate.
cues.zh: 但实际上，我觉得叫不定式更好。

cues.en: Indeterminate
cues.zh: 不定式

cues.en: would be a better word. Why do I say that? Well, here's an interesting thing.
cues.zh: 会是更合适的词。为什么这么说？来看一个有趣的现象。

cues.en: When we do arithmetic with small numbers,
cues.zh: 当我们用小数字做算术时，

cues.en: observe that if you add two small numbers, you expect the result to be a small number. If you multiply two small numbers, you expect the result to be a small number. Similarly,
cues.zh: 注意，两个小数字相加，结果应该是小数字。两个小数字相乘，结果也应该是小数字。同样，

cues.en: for division,
cues.zh: 对于除法，

cues.en: for subtraction,
cues.zh: 对于减法，

cues.en: the difference of two small numbers is a small number. On the other hand, the quotient of two small numbers is rather deceptive.
cues.zh: 两个小数字之差是小数字。另一方面，两个小数字之商却很具有迷惑性。

cues.en: Because it's a ratio, if one of the very small numbers happens to be very much larger compared with the other small number, the ratio might be quite large.
cues.zh: 因为这是个比值，如果其中一个很小的数恰好比另一个小得多的数大很多，比值就可能相当大。

cues.en: Well, for example, visualize,
cues.zh: 举个例子，想象一下，

cues.en: say, 10 to the minus six,
cues.zh: 比如说，10的负6次方，

cues.en: one one millionth.
cues.zh: 也就是百万分之一。

cues.en: You see, point zero zero zero zero zero one, which is a pretty small number. Now divide that by 10
cues.zh: 你看，0.000001，这是相当小的数。现在把它除以10的

cues.en: to the minus twelfth.
cues.zh: 负12次方。

cues.en: Well, you see, 10 to the minus twelfth is a small number, so small that it makes 10 to the minus sixth appear large. In fact, the quotient is
cues.zh: 你看，10的负12次方是个很小的数，小到让10的负6次方显得很大。事实上，商是

cues.en: 10 to the sixth,
cues.zh: 10的6次方，

cues.en: which is a million. And here we see that when you're dealing with the ratio of small numbers, you're a little bit in trouble because we can't tell whether the ratio will be small or large or somewhere in between. For example, if we reverse the role of numerator and denominator here, we would still have the quotient of two small numbers,
cues.zh: 也就是一百万。这里我们看到，当处理小数的比值时，会有点麻烦，因为我们无法判断比值是小还是大，或者介于两者之间。比如，如果我们把这里的分子和分母对调，仍然会得到两个小数的商，

cues.en: but 10 to the minus twelfth divided by 10 to the minus sixth
cues.zh: 但10的负12次方除以10的负6次方

cues.en: is a relatively small number, 10 to the minus six.
cues.zh: 是个相对较小的数，10的负6次方。

cues.en: Of course, this is the physical way of looking at it. Small divided by small is indeterminate.
cues.zh: 当然，这是从物理角度看。小数除以小数是不确定的。

cues.en: We have a more rigorous way of looking at this if you want to see it from a mathematical structure point of view. Namely, suppose we define
cues.zh: 如果想从数学结构的角度来看，我们有更严谨的方式。也就是，假设我们按

cues.en: a over b in the traditional way. Namely, a over b is that number such that when we multiply it by b, we get a.
cues.zh: 传统方式定义a除以b。即，a除以b是这样一个数：当它乘以b时，我们得到a。

cues.en: Well, what would that say as far as zero over zero was concerned? It would say what? That zero over zero is that number such that when we multiply it by zero, we get zero.
cues.zh: 那么，对于0除以0，这该怎么说？它会说0除以0是这样一个数：当它乘以0时，我们得到0。

cues.en: Now, what number has the property that when we multiply it by zero, we get zero? And the answer is any number.
cues.zh: 那么，什么数具有这样的性质：乘以零等于零？答案是任何数。

cues.en: This is why zero over zero is indeterminate. If we say to a person, tell me the number I must multiply by zero to get zero, the answer is any number.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么零除以零是不确定的。如果我们对一个人说，告诉我必须乘以零才能得到零的数是多少，答案是任何数。

cues.en: Well, the idea then is that we must avoid the expression zero over zero at all costs.
cues.zh: 那么，想法就是我们必须不惜一切代价避免零除以零这个表达式。

cues.en: What this means then is that we say, Okay, let the observers get closer and closer together, but never touch.
cues.zh: 这意味着我们说，好吧，让观察者越来越接近，但永不接触。

cues.en: Now, the point is that as long as the observers get closer and closer together and never touch, let's ask the question, how many pairs of observers do we need? And the answer is that theoretically,
cues.zh: 关键在于，只要观察者越来越接近且永不接触，让我们问这个问题：我们需要多少对观察者？从理论上讲，

cues.en: we need infinitely many pairs of observers.
cues.zh: 我们需要无限多对观察者。

cues.en: Well, why is that? Because as long as there's a distance between a pair of observers, we can theoretically
cues.zh: 为什么呢？因为只要一对观察者之间存在距离，理论上我们就能

cues.en: fit in another pair of observers.
cues.zh: 再放入另一对观察者。

cues.en: This is why in our course, we do not begin with this idea,
cues.zh: 这就是为什么在我们的课程中，我们不从这个想法开始，

cues.en: but looking backwards now, we say, ah, we had better find some way of giving us the equivalent of having infinitely many pairs of observers.
cues.zh: 但回过头来看，我们说，啊，我们最好找到某种方法，给我们等同于拥有无限多对观察者的效果。

cues.en: And to do this,
cues.zh: 为此，

cues.en: the idea that we come up with is the concept called a function.
cues.zh: 我们想到的主意就是称为函数的概念。

cues.en: Consider the old Galileo
cues.zh: 考虑古老的伽利略

cues.en: freely falling body problem,
cues.zh: 自由落体问题，

cues.en: where the distance that the body falls, s, equals 16 t squared, where t is in seconds and s is in feet.
cues.zh: 其中物体下落的距离s等于16t的平方，t以秒为单位，s以英尺为单位。

cues.en: Notice that this apparently harmless recipe
cues.zh: 注意，这个看似无害的配方

cues.en: gives us a way for finding s for each given t. In other words, to all intents and purposes, this recipe
cues.zh: 给了我们一种方法，对每个给定的t求出s。换句话说，实际上这个配方

cues.en: gives us an observer for each point
cues.zh: 为每个时间点

cues.en: of time.
cues.zh: 给了我们一个观察者。

cues.en: See, for each time, we can find a distance, which is physically equivalent to knowing an observer at every point.
cues.zh: 你看，对每个时刻，我们都能求出一个距离；这在物理上相当于在每个点都有一个观察者。

cues.en: In turn, the study of functions
cues.zh: 反过来，对函数的研究

cues.en: lends itself to a study of graphs, a picture.
cues.zh: 自然延伸到对图像的研究，也就是一幅图。

cues.en: Namely,
cues.zh: 也就是说，

cues.en: if we look at s equals 16 t squared again, notice that we visualize
cues.zh: 如果我们再看 s = 16t²，注意我们会把

cues.en: recipe here. T can be viewed as being an input. S is the output.
cues.zh: 这里的做法可视化。T 可看作输入，S 是输出。

cues.en: For a given input t, we can compute the output s.
cues.zh: 给定输入 t，我们就能算出输出 s。

cues.en: In general, if we now elect to plot the input input along a horizontal line
cues.zh: 一般来说，如果我们现在选择把输入沿水平线画出

cues.en: and the output at right angles to this, we now have a picture of our relationship,
cues.zh: 再把输出沿与它垂直的方向画出，我们就得到了两者关系的图像，

cues.en: a picture which is called a graph.
cues.zh: 这幅图称为图像。

cues.en: You see, we can talk about this more explicitly as far as this particular problem is concerned just by taking a look at a picture like this. In other words, in this particular problem,
cues.zh: 你看，就这个特定问题而言，只要看看这样一幅图，我们就能更明确地讨论它。换句话说，在这个问题中，

cues.en: the input is time, t. The output is distance, s.
cues.zh: 输入是时间 t，输出是距离 s。

cues.en: For each t, we locate a height called s by squaring t and multiplying by 16.
cues.zh: 对每个 t，我们通过把 t 平方再乘以 16，确定一个称为 s 的高度。

cues.en: And now, what average speed means in terms of this kind of a diagram is the following. To find the average speed, all we have to do is on a given time interval,
cues.zh: 那么，在这种图上，平均速度的含义如下。要求平均速度，我们只需在给定的时间区间上，

cues.en: find the distance traveled, which I call delta s, the change in distance, and divide that by the change in time. That's the average speed, which by the way, from a geometrical
cues.zh: 求出走过的距离，我称之为 Δs，也就是距离的变化量，再除以时间的变化量。这就是平均速度；顺便说，从几何

cues.en: point of view, becomes known as the slope of this particular straight line. In other words, average speed is to functions
cues.zh: 角度看，它就成了这条特定直线的斜率。换句话说，平均速度之于函数，

cues.en: what slope of a straight line is to geometry.
cues.zh: 就像直线的斜率之于几何。

cues.en: At any rate, knowing what the average rate of speed is, we sort of say, why couldn't we define the instantaneous
cues.zh: 不管怎样，知道了平均速度是多少，我们就会说，为什么不能把瞬时

cues.en: speed to be this? We will take the change in distance
cues.zh: 速度定义成这样呢？我们就取距离的变化量

cues.en: divided by the change in time
cues.zh: 除以时间的变化量

cues.en: and see what happens, and we write this this way, limit as delta t approaches zero, let's see what happens as that change in time becomes arbitrarily small,
cues.zh: 看看会发生什么，我们这样写，当 delta t 趋近于零时的极限，看看当时间变化量变得任意小的时候会发生什么，

cues.en: but never equaling zero because we don't want a zero over zero form here. You see, this then becomes
cues.zh: 但永远不等于零，因为我们不想在这里出现零除以零的形式。你看，这就成了

cues.en: the working definition
cues.zh: 我们所谓的微分学的

cues.en: of what we call differential calculus.
cues.zh: 工作定义。

cues.en: The point is that this particular definition
cues.zh: 关键在于，这个特定的定义

cues.en: does not depend on s equaling 16 t squared.
cues.zh: 并不依赖于 s 等于 16 t 平方。

cues.en: S could be any
cues.zh: s 可以是 t 的

cues.en: function of t whatsoever.
cues.zh: 任何函数。

cues.en: We could have a more elaborate type of situation.
cues.zh: 我们可以有更复杂的情况。

cues.en: The important point is what?
cues.zh: 重点是什么呢？

cues.zh: 这门学科最终被称为积分学，

cues.zh: 我们想求的就是区域r的面积。古希腊人对这种求面积的方法有个挺有趣的称呼。我觉得它既是比喻也是字面意思。它叫穷竭法。

cues.en: What they did was to ins... They would divide the interval, say, into n equal parts.
cues.zh: 他们的做法是……他们把区间分成n等份。

cues.en: And picking the lowest point in each interval,
cues.zh: 在每个区间里取最低点，

cues.zh: 然后内接

cues.en: a rectangle.
cues.zh: 一个矩形。

cues.en: They would... Knowing that the area of the rectangle was the base times the height, they would add up the area of each of these rectangles
cues.zh: 他们……知道矩形面积是底乘高，就把这些矩形的面积加起来，

cues.en: and know that whatever that area was, that would have to be too small to be the right answer because that region was contained in R. And that would be labeled a sub n lower bar, say, to indicate that this was a sum of rectangles which was too small to be the right answer.
cues.zh: 并且知道无论这个面积是多少，它肯定太小，不可能是正确答案，因为那个区域包含在R里面。这个可以记作下和s_n，表示这是矩形之和，太小了，不是正确答案。

cues.en: Similarly,
cues.zh: 同理，

cues.zh: 他们随后会找到最高点

cues.en: in each rectangle,
cues.zh: 在每个矩形中，

cues.en: get an over approximation by adding up the sum of those areas, which they would call a sub n upper bar, and now know that the area of the region that they were looking for was squeezed in between these two, then what they would do is make more and more divisions.
cues.zh: 通过把这些面积相加得到一个上近似，他们称之为 sub n upper bar，现在知道他们要找的区域面积被挤压在这两者之间，然后他们会做越来越多的划分。

cues.en: And hopefully,
cues.zh: 希望如此，

cues.en: and I think you can see this sort of intuitively happening here, each of the lower approximations
cues.zh: 我想你能直观地看到这里发生的情况，每个下近似

cues.en: and shops off the space from outside here. And hopefully,
cues.zh: 并从外部削减空间。希望如此，

cues.en: if both of these
cues.zh: 如果这两个

cues.en: bounds
cues.zh: 界限

cues.en: sort of converge to the same value l, we get the idea that the area of the region r must be l.
cues.zh: 都收敛到同一个值 l，我们就得到区域 r 的面积必须是 l 的概念。

cues.en: This is not anything new. In other words, this is a technique that is some 2,500
cues.zh: 这并不新鲜。换句话说，这是一种大约有 2,500

cues.en: Of course, what happens with engineering students in general is that one frequently says, but I'm not interested in studying area. I am not a geometer.

cues.en: What good is the area under a curve? And the interesting point here becomes that if we label
cues.zh: 曲线下的面积有什么用？有趣的一点是，如果我们标记

cues.en: the coordinate axes rather than x and y, give them physical labels, it turns out that area under a curve has a physical interpretation.
cues.zh: 坐标轴而不是 x 和 y，给它们物理标签，事实证明曲线下的面积有物理解释。

cues.en: Consider the same problem, only now instead of talking about y equals x squared, let's talk about v, the velocity, equaling the square of the time, and say that the time goes from zero to one. In other words,
cues.zh: 考虑同样的问题，只是现在不谈 y 等于 x 的平方，而是谈 v，速度，等于时间的平方，并说时间从零到一。换句话说，

cues.en: if we plot v versus t, we get a picture like this. And the question that comes up is, what do we mean by the area under the curve here? And again, without belaboring this point, not because it's not important,
cues.zh: 如果我们绘制 v 对 t 的图，我们会得到这样的图。出现的问题是，这里的曲线下面积是什么意思？再次，不赘述这一点，不是因为不重要，

cues.zh: 而是因为这只是概述，我们会在课程后面回到所有这些主题。

cues.en: The point I just want to bring out here is, notice that the area under the curve here is the distance that this particle would travel moving at this speed
cues.zh: 我刚想在这里强调的是，注意这条曲线下方的面积，就是这个粒子以这个速度运动所会走的距离

cues.en: if the time goes from zero to one. And notice what we're saying here. Again,
cues.zh: 如果时间从零到一的话。注意我们在这里说的是。再说一遍，

cues.en: suppose we divide this interval into n equal parts
cues.zh: 假设我们把这个区间分成 n 等份

cues.en: and inscribe
cues.zh: 然后内接

cues.zh: 看，在这段时间上，曲线下方的面积就是它在这段时间间隔内走过的距离。间隔。换句话说，我们要说的是，如果粒子以这个速度从此时运动到此时，然后以这个速度

In other words, in the same way as before that the area of the region R
cues.zh: 这小于粒子真正走过的距离，因为注意，粒子在从这儿到这儿每一瞬间的速度都大于这个，在从这儿到这儿每一瞬间的速度都大于这个。换句话说，和之前一样，区域 R 的面积

cues.en: And these two things,
cues.zh: 这两件事，

cues.en: namely what? Instantaneous speed and area under a curve are the two essential branches of calculus.
cues.zh: 具体来说是什么？瞬时速度和曲线下面积是微积分的两个核心分支。

cues.en: Differential calculus being concerned with instantaneous rate of speed,
cues.zh: 微分学关注的是瞬时速度，

cues.en: integral calculus with area under a curve.
cues.zh: 微积分中曲线下的面积。

cues.en: And the beauty of calculus,
cues.zh: 而微积分的美妙之处在于，

cues.en: surprisingly enough,
cues.zh: 令人惊讶的是，

cues.en: in a way, is only secondary as far as these two topics are concerned. The true beauty lies in the fact that these apparently

cues.en: two different branches of calculus,
cues.zh: 微积分的两个不同分支，

cues.zh: 其中一项早在公元前600年就由古希腊人发明了，

cues.zh: 它们之间通过一个相当引人注目的东西联系在一起。这个引人注目的东西，我们将在课程中着重强调，

cues.en: is that areas and rates of change are related by area under a curve. Now, I don't know how to draw this so that you can see this thing as vividly as possible,
cues.zh: 关键就在于面积和变化率通过曲线下的面积联系在一起。我不知道该怎么画，才能让你们尽可能直观地看到这一点，

cues.en: but the idea is this. Think of area being swept out as we take a line and move it, tracing out the curve this way, towards the right. Notice that if we have a certain amount of area,
cues.zh: 但核心思路是这样的。想象我们拿一条线向右移动来描绘出曲线，随之扫过的就是面积。注意，如果我们有特定大小的面积，

cues.en: if we have a certain amount of area, if we now move a little bit further to the right, notice that
cues.zh: 如果我们有了一定的面积，现在再稍微往右移一点，就会发现

cues.en: the new area,
cues.zh: 新领域，

cues.en: the new area somehow depends
cues.zh: 新领域在某种程度上取决于

cues.en: on what the height of this curve is going to be.
cues.zh: 这取决于这条曲线的高度会是多少。

cues.zh: 这似乎表明，曲线下的面积必定存在某种关联

cues.en: to how fast
cues.zh: 到多快

cues.zh: 这条线的高度在变。

cues.en: Or to look at it inversely,
cues.zh: 反过来看，

cues.en: how fast the area is changing should somehow be related to the height of this line.

cues.en: And just what that relationship is will be explored also in great detail in the course, and we will show the beautiful marriage between this differential
cues.zh: 而这个关系究竟是什么，课程中也会详细探讨，我们会展示微分

cues.en: and integral calculus through this relationship here, which becomes known as the fundamental theorem of integral calculus.
cues.zh: 与积分之间通过这里这个关系实现的完美结合，这个关系后来被称为积分学基本定理。

cues.en: At any rate then, what this should show us is that calculus
cues.zh: 无论如何，这应该向我们表明，微积分

cues.en: hinges whether it's
cues.zh: 无论是

cues.en: differential calculus or integral calculus,
cues.zh: 微分学还是积分学，

cues.en: that calculus hinges on something called the limit concept.
cues.zh: 微积分都依赖于一个叫做极限的概念。

cues.en: Again, by way of a very quick review,
cues.zh: 再次快速回顾一下，

cues.en: one of the limit concepts, and I think it's easy to see geometrically rather than analytically,
cues.zh: 其中一个极限概念，我觉得从几何上比从解析上更容易看出来，

cues.en: imagine that we have a curve
cues.zh: 想象我们有一条曲线

cues.en: and we wanna find the tangent to the curve at the point p.
cues.zh: 我们想找到曲线在点 p 处的切线。

cues.en: What we can do is is take a point q and draw the straight line that joins p to q.
cues.zh: 我们可以做的是取一个点 q，画一条连接 p 和 q 的直线。

cues.en: We can then find the slope of the line p q.
cues.zh: 然后我们可以求出直线 p q 的斜率。

cues.en: The trouble is that p q does not look very much like the tangent line, so we say, Okay, let q move down so it comes closer to p. We can then find the slopes of p q one. We can find the slope of p q two.
cues.zh: 问题在于 p q 看起来不太像切线，于是我们说，好，让 q 往下移动，靠近 p。然后我们可以求出 p q 一的斜率，求出 p q 二的斜率。

cues.en: But in each case, we still do not have the slope
cues.zh: 但每种情况下，我们仍然没有得到

cues.en: of the line tangent to the curve at p. But we get the idea that as q gets closer and closer to p,
cues.zh: 曲线在 p 处切线的斜率。但我们有了这样的想法：当 q 越来越接近 p 时，

cues.en: the slope of the secant line that joins p to q becomes a better and better approximation
cues.zh: 连接 p 和 q 的割线斜率会越来越好地近似

cues.en: to the line that would be tangent to the curve at p.
cues.zh: 曲线在 p 处的切线。

cues.en: In fact, it's rather interesting
cues.zh: 事实上，这相当有趣

cues.en: that in the sixteenth century,
cues.zh: 在十六世纪，

cues.en: the definition that was given of a tangent line was that a tangent line is a line which passes through two
cues.zh: 切线的定义是：切线是一条穿过曲线上两个

cues.en: consecutive
cues.zh: 连续

cues.en: points on a curve. Now, obviously, a curve does not have two consecutive points.
cues.zh: 点的直线。但显然，一条曲线并没有两个连续的点。

cues.en: What they really meant was what? That as q gets closer and closer to p,
cues.zh: 他们真正想表达的是什么呢？当 q 越来越靠近 p 时，

cues.en: the secant line becomes
cues.zh: 割线就成了

cues.en: approximation for the tangent line.
cues.zh: 切线的近似。

cues.en: And that, in a way, if the two points were allowed to coincide,
cues.zh: 从某种意义上说，如果允许这两个点重合，

cues.en: that should give us the perfect answer. The trouble is, just like you can't divide zero by zero, if p and q coincide,
cues.zh: 那应该就能给出完美的答案。问题在于，就像你不能用零除以零一样，如果 p 和 q 重合，

cues.en: how many points do you have?
cues.zh: 你还有几个点？

cues.en: Just one point, and it takes two points to determine a straight line. No matter how close q is to p, we have two distinct points. As soon as q touches p, we lose this. And this is what was meant by ancient man, or medieval man, by his notion of two consecutive points. And I should put this in double quotes because I think you can see what he's begging to try to say
cues.zh: 只有一个点，而确定一条直线需要两个点。无论 q 离 p 多近，我们都有两个不同的点。一旦 q 碰到 p，我们就失去了这个条件。这就是古人或中世纪人所说的“两个连续点”的含义。我应该把这个词加上双引号，因为我想你能看出他想用“连续”这个词

cues.en: with the word consecutive even though from a purely rigorous point of view, this has no geometric meaning.
cues.zh: 表达什么，尽管从纯粹严谨的角度来看，这个词并没有几何意义。

cues.en: Now, the other form of limit has to do with adding up areas of rectangles on the curves.
cues.zh: 现在，另一种形式的极限与累加曲线上矩形的面积有关。

cues.en: Namely, we divide the curve up into n parts,
cues.zh: 也就是，我们把曲线分成 n 份，

cues.en: we inscribe
cues.zh: 内接

cues.en: rectangles,
cues.zh: 矩形，

cues.en: and then we let n increase without bound. In other words, this is sort of a discrete type of limit,
cues.zh: 然后让 n 无限增大。换句话说，这是一种离散型的极限，

cues.en: namely, we must add up a whole number of areas,
cues.zh: 即我们必须累加整数个面积，

cues.en: but the sum is endless
cues.zh: 但这个和是无穷的

cues.en: in the sense that the number of rectangles
cues.zh: 意思是矩形的数量

cues.en: becomes greater than any number we want to pre assign.

cues.en: And the basic question that we must contend with here,
cues.zh: 那么我们必须面对的基本问题是，

cues.en: the basic question that we must contend with here is how big is an infinite sum? You see, when we say infinite sum, that just tells you how many terms you're combining. It doesn't tell you how big each term, how big the sum will be. For example, look at the following sum. I will start with one,
cues.zh: 这里我们要面对的基本问题是：一个无穷和到底有多大？你看，当我们说无穷和时，那只是告诉你把多少项加在一起，并没有告诉你每一项有多大，和会有多大。举个例子，看下面这个和。我先从 1 开始，

cues.en: then I'll add a half on twice,
cues.zh: 然后加两次二分之一，

cues.en: then I'll add a third on
cues.zh: 再加三次三分之一，

cues.en: three times,
cues.zh: 三次，

cues.en: and without belaboring this this point, let me then say I'll add on a fourth four times, a fifth five times, a sixth six times, etcetera.
cues.zh: 不啰嗦这一点，我接着说，再加四次四分之一、五次五分之一、六次六分之一，以此类推。

cues.en: Notice as I do this,
cues.zh: 注意，当我这样做时，

cues.en: that each time the terms get smaller,
cues.zh: 每一项都变得越来越小，

cues.en: yet the sum increases
cues.zh: 但和却增长

cues.en: without any bound. Namely, notice that this adds up to one, this adds up to one, the next four terms will add up to one. And as I go out further and further,
cues.zh: 没有任何上界。也就是说，注意这一组加起来是 1，这一组加起来是 1，接下来四项加起来也会是 1。随着我越往后加，

cues.en: notice that this sum can become as great as I want just by me adding on enough ones.
cues.zh: 注意，只要我加上足够多的 1，这个和就能想多大就多大。

cues.en: On the other hand, let's look at this one. One plus a half plus a quarter plus an eighth plus a sixteenth
cues.zh: 另一方面，看看这个。1 加二分之一加四分之一加八分之一加十六分之一

cues.en: plus a thirty second. In other words, I start with one and each time add on half the previous number. See, one plus a half plus a quarter plus an eighth. You may remember this as being the geometric series
cues.zh: 加三十二分之一。换句话说，我从 1 开始，每次加上前一个数的一半。看，1 加二分之一加四分之一加八分之一。你可能记得这是等比级数，

cues.en: whose ratio is one half.
cues.zh: 公比是二分之一。

cues.en: The interesting thing is
cues.zh: 有趣的是，

cues.en: that now this sum gets as close to two as you want without ever getting there. And rather than prove this right now, let's just look at a geometric interpretation here.
cues.zh: 现在这个和可以任意接近 2，却永远到不了 2。与其现在就证明这一点，不如先看一个几何解释。

cues.en: Take a line which is two inches long.
cues.zh: 假设有一条两英寸长的线段。

cues.en: Suppose you first go halfway.
cues.zh: 假设你先走一半。

cues.en: You're now here.
cues.zh: 你现在到了这里。

cues.en: Now go half the remaining distance. That's what? One plus a half. That puts you over here.
cues.zh: 现在再走剩下距离的一半。那是多少？一加上二分之一。这就到了这里。

cues.en: Now go half the remaining distance.
cues.zh: 现在再走剩下距离的一半。

cues.en: That means add on a quarter.
cues.zh: 也就是再加上四分之一。

cues.en: Now go half the remaining distance. That means add on an eighth. Now go half the remaining distance. Add up on a sixteenth, you see. And ultimately, what happens? Well, no matter where you stop, you've become closer and closer to two without ever getting there. And as you go further and further, you can get as close to two as you want. In other words, here are infinitely many terms whose infinite sum is two. Here are infinitely many terms whose infinite sum is
cues.zh: 现在再走剩下距离的一半。也就是再加上八分之一。现在再走剩下距离的一半。你看，再加上十六分之一。最终会发生什么？无论你在哪里停下，你都越来越接近二，却永远无法真正到达。而只要你一直走下去，你想多接近二就能多接近二。换句话说，这里有无穷多个项，它们的无穷和是二。这里有无穷多个项，它们的无穷和——

cues.en: infinity, we should say, because it increases without bound. And this was the problem that hung up the ancient Greek. How could you do infinitely many things in a finite amount of time? In fact,
cues.zh: 严格来说是无穷大，因为它在无上限地增长。古希腊人正是被这个问题困扰住了：你怎么可能在有限的时间里做完无穷多件事？事实上，

cues.en: at the same time that the Greek was developing integral calculus, the famous Greek philosopher Zeno
cues.zh: 就在希腊人发展积分学的同时，著名的希腊哲学家 Zeno

cues.en: was working on things called Zeno's paradoxes.
cues.zh: 正在研究所谓的“Zeno 悖论”。

cues.en: And Zeno's paradoxes
cues.zh: Zeno 悖论

cues.en: are three in number, of which I only want to quote one here, but it's a paradox which shows how Zeno could not visualize quite what was happening.
cues.zh: 一共有三个，这里我只想提其中一个，这个悖论表明 Zeno 当时并不能完全想明白实际发生了什么。

cues.en: You see, it's called the tortoise and the hare problem.
cues.zh: 你看，它就是“龟兔赛跑”问题。

cues.en: Suppose that you give the tortoise
cues.zh: 假设你让乌龟

cues.en: a one yard head start on the hare.
cues.zh: 比兔子先跑一码。

cues.en: And suppose, for the sake of argument, just to mimic the problem that we were doing before, suppose it's a slow hare and a fast tortoise so that the hare only runs twice as fast as the tortoise.
cues.zh: 假设为了讨论方便，就模拟我们之前做的那个问题，假设这是一只慢兔子和一只快乌龟，兔子的速度只有乌龟的两倍。

cues.en: You see, Zeno's paradox says that the hare can never catch the tortoise. Why? Because that's... To catch the tortoise, the hare must first go the one yard head start that the tortoise had.
cues.zh: 你看，芝诺悖论说兔子永远追不上乌龟。为什么？因为要追上乌龟，兔子必须先跑完乌龟领先的那一码。

cues.en: Well, by the time the hare gets here, the tortoise has gone a half yard because the tortoise travels half as fast. Now the hare must make up the half yard. But while the hare makes up the half yard,
cues.zh: 等兔子跑到这儿，乌龟已经跑了半码，因为乌龟的速度是兔子的一半。现在兔子必须追回这半码。但当兔子追回这半码时，

cues.en: the tortoise goes a quarter of a yard. When the hare makes up the quarter of a yard, the tortoise goes an eighth of a yard. And so Zeno argues the hare gets closer and closer to the tortoise
cues.zh: 乌龟又跑了四分之一码。当兔子追回这四分之一码时，乌龟又跑了八分之一码。芝诺由此论证，兔子会越来越接近乌龟，

cues.en: but can't catch him. And this, of course, is a rather strange thing because Zeno knew
cues.zh: 但永远追不上它。这当然是一件相当奇怪的事，因为芝诺知道

cues.en: that the tortoise would catch the hare. That's why it's called a paradox. A paradox means something which appears to be true, yet is obviously false.
cues.zh: 乌龟会被兔子追上。这就是为什么它被称为悖论。悖论意味着某种看似为真、却显然为假的东西。

cues.en: Now, that we can resolve Zeno's paradox into the example we were just talking about.
cues.zh: 现在，我们可以把芝诺悖论化解为我们刚才讨论的那个例子。

cues.en: Argument, notice what's happening here with the time. For the sake of argument, let's suppose that the tortoise travels at one yard per second. Then what you're saying is I mean, the hare travels at one yard per second. What you're saying is it takes the hare one second to go this distance.
cues.zh: 论证，注意这里时间上发生了什么。为了讨论方便，假设乌龟每秒跑一码。那么你所说的就是，我的意思是，兔子每秒跑一码。你所说的是，兔子跑完这段距离需要一秒。

cues.en: Then it takes them a half a second to go this distance. Then a quarter of a second to go this distance. And what you're saying is is that as he's gaining on the tortoise,
cues.zh: 然后它需要半秒走完这段距离，再用四分之一秒走完这段距离。而你要说的是，随着它逐渐追上乌龟，

cues.en: these are the time intervals which transpiring.
cues.zh: 这些就是正在流逝的时间间隔。

cues.en: And this sum turns out to be
cues.zh: 而这个和结果是

cues.en: two.
cues.zh: 二。

cues.en: Now, of course, those of us who had eighth grade algebra know an easier way of solving this problem. We say, look at, let's solve this problem algebraically.
cues.zh: 当然，我们这些学过八年级代数的人知道解这个问题的更简单方法。我们说，看，让我们用代数方法解这个问题。

cues.en: Namely, we say, give
cues.zh: 也就是说，我们说，给

cues.en: the tortoise a one yard head start.
cues.zh: 乌龟一码的领先优势。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: call x the distance
cues.zh: 令x为距离

cues.en: or the point at which the hare catches the tortoise.
cues.zh: 或兔子追上乌龟的那个点。

cues.en: Now, the hare is traveling one yard per second.
cues.zh: 现在，兔子每秒跑一码。

cues.en: The tortoise is traveling a half a yard per second.
cues.zh: 乌龟每秒跑半码。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好吗？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: if we take distance,
cues.zh: 如果我们取距离，

cues.en: the distance traveled,
cues.zh: 走过的距离，

cues.en: and divide it by the rate,
cues.zh: 除以速率，

cues.en: that should be
cues.zh: 那应该是

cues.en: the time.
cues.zh: 时间。

cues.en: And since they both are at this point at the same time, we get what? X over one equals x minus one divided by onetwo.
cues.zh: 既然它们同时到达这个点，我们得到什么？x除以一等于x减一除以二分之一。

cues.en: And assuming as a prerequisite that we have had algebra,
cues.zh: 并且假设作为前提我们已经学过代数，

cues.en: it follows almost trivially that x equals two.
cues.zh: 几乎显然可以推出x等于二。

cues.en: In other words, what this says is, in reality,
cues.zh: 换句话说，这说明的是，在现实中，

cues.en: that the hare will not overtake the tortoise until he catches him,
cues.zh: 兔子在追上乌龟之前不会超过它，

cues.en: which is obvious.
cues.zh: 这是显而易见的。

cues.en: But what's not so obvious is what? That these infinitely many terms can add up to a finite sum.
cues.zh: 但不太明显的是什么？这些无穷多个项可以加起来得到一个有限的和。

cues.en: Well, at any rate, this completes the overview
cues.zh: 好吧，无论如何，这就完成了概述

cues.en: of what our course will be like. And to help you focus your attention on
cues.zh: 关于我们的课程会是什么样子。为了帮助你把注意力集中在

cues.en: what our course really says, what we shall do computationally
cues.zh: 我们课程真正要讲的内容，我们在计算上要做的是

cues.en: is this.
cues.zh: 这个。

cues.en: In review, we shall start with functions,
cues.zh: 回顾一下，我们从函数开始，

cues.en: and functions involve the modern concept of sets because they're
cues.zh: 而函数涉及现代集合的概念，因为它们是

cues.en: relationships between sets of objects.
cues.zh: 对象集合之间的关系。

cues.en: We will talk about limits,
cues.zh: 我们会讲极限，

cues.en: derivatives,
cues.zh: 导数，

cues.en: rate of change,
cues.zh: 变化率，

cues.en: integrals,
cues.zh: 积分，

cues.en: area under curves. This will be our fundamental building block.
cues.zh: 曲线下的面积。这将是我们最基础的构建模块。

cues.en: Once this is done,
cues.zh: 一旦这些讲完，

cues.en: these things will never change, but the remainder of our course will be to talk about applications,
cues.zh: 这些东西永远不会变，但我们课程剩下的部分将讨论应用，

cues.en: which is the name of the game as far as engineering is concerned.
cues.zh: 就工程而言，这才是关键所在。

cues.en: More elaborate functions, namely, how do we handle tougher relationships?
cues.zh: 更复杂的函数，也就是我们如何处理更难的关系？

cues.en: Related to the tougher relationships
cues.zh: 与更难的关系相关，

cues.en: will come more sophisticated techniques.
cues.zh: 会有更精细的技巧。

cues.en: And finally, we will conclude our course with the topic that we were just talking about, infinite series, how do we get a hold of what happens when you add up infinitely many things, each of which gets small.
cues.zh: 最后，我们将以刚刚谈到的主题——无穷级数——来结束课程，也就是当你把无穷多个越来越小的东西加起来时，如何把握其结果。

cues.en: At any rate, that concludes our lecture for today.
cues.zh: 总之，今天的课就到这里。

cues.en: We will have a digression in the sense that the next few lessons will consist
cues.zh: 我们会稍作岔开，接下来的几节课将包含

cues.en: of sets,
cues.zh: 集合，

cues.en: things that you can read about at your leisure in our supplementary notes.
cues.zh: 这些内容你们可以在补充讲义中闲暇时阅读。

cues.en: Learn to understand these because the concept of a set is the building block, the fundamental language of modern mathematics,
cues.zh: 要学会理解这些，因为集合的概念是构建模块，是现代数学的基本语言，

cues.en: and then we will return once we have sets underway to talk about functions,
cues.zh: 等集合讲清楚后，我们会回到函数的话题，

cues.en: and then we will build gradually from there.
cues.zh: 然后从那里逐步展开。

cues.en: Hopefully, when our course ends, we will have in slow motion gone through today's lesson.
cues.zh: 希望课程结束时，我们能以慢动作走完今天的课。

cues.en: This completes our presentation for today, and until next time, goodbye.
cues.zh: 今天的演讲就到这里，下次见，再见。
